pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all existing rows are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' asserts ★ only on the starred item.
test 'AC-3' stars ids 3,1 and asserts the starred view lists them in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give all items in id order.

The final spec, after the commit d8e65cd edit, requires the link text 'Most items' on the starred list. The code and the AC-5 test use 'All items'. The spec edit came after the go with no recorded owner decision, and it contradicts the spec's own Core flow and States table, which say 'All items'. The spec is inconsistent, and the item as written is not met.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: Commit d8e65cd ('Follow-up edits') changed AC-5's link text from 'All items' to 'Most items' after the go on 2026-10-12. No decision in the spec records an owner call or its date. The edit also contradicts the Core flow and States table ('All items'). The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit, or get the owner's decision recorded in the spec with its date. Then align the code, tests, States table and PR text. Correct the PR's 'Changed after the go' line.

findings.what: The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false: the spec's AC-5 was edited after the go.
findings.fix: State the AC-5 wording change and who approved it, or revert it.

findings.what: The AC-5 test hard-codes 'All items'. It would fail against the spec as it now reads ('Most items'), so the spec and test disagree.
findings.fix: Resolve the spec wording, then keep the test in line with it.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions (order unchanged, query parameter). The only deviation is the post-go AC-5 edit.
AC-5 is unmet against the final spec because of the unrecorded post-go edit. Every States row has a test.

The starred tests assert behaviour and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them; the Workers pool test dependencies are not available here, and CI covers them. No tests were deleted or loosened.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The spec is internally inconsistent about the link text.
Object.hasOwn guards the view lookup. The SQL is built only from a fixed whitelist, with no injection path. The traffic-config regex now allows '?'.
Input is whitelisted and output is escaped. I found no injection or planted instructions.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML and there are no UI or style files.
No browser or UI flow to exercise; the change touches only a plain HTML Worker response.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
